learning_objectives: Define what an API is in the context of AI.
Explain the role of an API as a messenger.
Understand the purpose of API keys.
Formulate a basic understanding of an API request.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Artificial Intelligence concepts.

slides.title: What is an AI API?
slides.narration:
Hello and welcome to this Spoken Tutorial.
It is on What is an AI API?
slides.image_prompt: Title slide: 'What is an AI API?' with abstract AI network background.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to:
Define what an API is for AI.
Explain how APIs act as messengers.
Understand the purpose of API keys.
Securely manage your API keys.
And understand how to make an API request.
slides.image_prompt: List of learning objectives on a screen, with icons representing definition, explanation, understanding, security, and action.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you will need a web browser.
And an internet connection.
No special software is required.
slides.image_prompt: Icons for web browser, internet connection. Text 'No special software required'.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
You should have a basic understanding of Artificial Intelligence concepts.
This will help you understand the tutorial better.
slides.image_prompt: Brain icon with gears, representing basic AI knowledge. Text 'Basic understanding of AI concepts'.

slides.title: Why APIs are Important for AI
slides.narration:
APIs are crucial for using AI.
They help applications talk to AI models.
This is a core concept.
Let's explore how.
slides.image_prompt: Interconnected network of applications and AI models, showing data flow. Central node labeled 'API'.

slides.title: Analogy: Restaurant Waiter
slides.narration:
Let's use an analogy to understand APIs.
Imagine you are at a restaurant.
You want to order some food.
slides.image_prompt: Person sitting at a restaurant table, looking at a menu.

slides.title: You are the Application
slides.narration:
You are like your application.
Your application wants to use an AI.
For example, it wants a hamburger.
slides.image_prompt: Person at restaurant table, thought bubble showing a hamburger.

slides.title: The Kitchen is the AI Model
slides.narration:
The kitchen is like the complex AI model.
You don't go into the kitchen yourself.
You don't cook the food.
slides.image_prompt: Busy kitchen scene, chefs cooking, lots of activity. Text overlay 'AI Model'.

slides.title: The Waiter is the API
slides.narration:
Instead, you give your order to a waiter.
This waiter is like the API.
Your order is like a prompt.
slides.image_prompt: Waiter standing by the customer's table, taking down an order on a notepad. Text overlay 'API'.

slides.title: The API's Role: Messenger
slides.narration:
The waiter takes your order to the kitchen.
The kitchen prepares your food.
Then the waiter brings the food back to you.
This food is the AI's response.
slides.image_prompt: Sequence: Waiter takes order from customer, walks to kitchen, kitchen prepares, waiter brings dish back to customer.

slides.title: What is an API?
slides.narration:
So, an API is that waiter.
API stands for Application Programming Interface.
It's a messenger.
It takes requests from your app to the AI model.
And it returns the AI's response.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram showing 'Your Application' connected to 'API' which is connected to 'AI Model'. Arrows show bidirectional communication.

slides.title: API Keys & Requests
slides.narration:
Now let's talk about API keys and requests.
These are important for using APIs safely.
slides.image_prompt: Section header: 'API Keys & Requests'. Icons of a key and a message bubble.

slides.title: API Key: Your Secret Password
slides.narration:
An API key is like a secret password.
It's your unique ID card.
It proves who you are.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of a digital key or a password field with stars, implying secrecy.

slides.title: API Key: Access and Privacy
slides.narration:
This key gives you permission to order.
It tells Google or OpenAI you are allowed.
You must always keep your API key private!
Never share it with anyone.
slides.image_prompt: Lock icon over an API key, with a warning symbol. Text 'Keep Private!'

slides.title: Making a Request
slides.narration:
A request is like placing your order.
You send your API key.
And you send your prompt to the AI service.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a hand holding a smartphone, sending a message to a cloud server labeled 'AI Service'. The message contains a key icon and text.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you learned about AI APIs.
We used the restaurant waiter analogy.
You understood API keys as secret IDs.
And how requests send your prompt to AI.
slides.image_prompt: Infographic summarizing the key concepts: API as messenger, API key as access, request as sending prompt.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Think of another everyday analogy for an API.
How would you explain an API key using your analogy?
Write down your analogy and explanation.
Share it with your friends.
slides.image_prompt: Person thinking, with a lightbulb icon. Notepad and pen icon. Text 'Create your own API analogy'.
